written: 2026-11-10, before R1's code and before either check ran on any table
about: R1 of protein v2 (research/value-scale-v2-plan.md, R1. The corpus checks). Two checks join B3's walk (valuescale/corpus/draw.py). (1) An empty table is refused as a walk outcome of its own, 'empty': a parsed table that holds no observed value, where observed means finite and not 0. The check comes after the walk's size checks (at least 20 columns and 200 rows) and before the label, so every outcome a table gets today is unchanged unless the table is empty. (2) A table the label calls linear whose observed values look log is flagged for the hand audit: 99% of its observed values under 64 (B7's LOG_CEILING, research/notebooks/value_scale_b7_posthoc.py). The kept record carries its value range (smallest, median, 99th percentile, largest); the label is not changed and nothing is refused. The audit's sample takes every flagged table besides its seeded share, and a flagged table's packet shows its value range beside its headers and methods. The predictions come from B7's post hoc read (research/notebook-outputs/value_scale_b7/posthoc.json, faulty_tables). On 2026-11-10 the three faulty tables' parsed values were opened once to confirm that account (both empty tables all missing; PXD066316 from 7.96 to 26.76), and a scratch probe sent the service tables with no observed value (below). No other table was looked at. Not edited after the run: a row that differs is reported and explained in notes.md.
tables: the 457 tables B3 kept (valuescale/corpus/walk.jsonl, outcome kept), each read from its parsed table (data/incoming/value-scale-corpus/<accession>/table.npz, the walk's own parse, stored as float32); and the bank's 37 tables (valuescale/corpus/bank.json), each whole, as the service's parser reads it (research/notebooks/value_scale_diagnostics.py, load_entry). No reserve deposit is listed and no sealed accession is opened.
R1_empty: the empty check fires on exactly 2 of the 457 kept tables: PXD022054 (MaxQuant, test) and PXD047898 (FragPipe, test)

R1_flag.what: the flag fires on exactly 1 of the 455 kept tables that are not empty (every kept table is labelled linear: B3 found no table labelled log)
R1_flag.predicted: PXD066316 (Spectronaut, test), its observed values from 7.96 to 26.76 with median 15.02, as posthoc.json records them to two decimals

R1_bank_empty: the empty check fires on none of the bank's 37 tables
R1_bank_control: a positive control: the flag's rule (99% of the observed values under 64), applied to the bank's 9 tables labelled log as if they were labelled linear, fires on all 9
R1_bank_linear: recorded, with no prediction and no pass or fail: which of the bank's 28 tables labelled linear the flag would send to the audit, with each one's range. They are real linear tables, so each is a table the audit would read and keep. The plan names pxd064083_t and pxd064083_b (median about 7) as the kind an automatic refusal by value range would have dropped

R1_service.what: an upload whose every entry is empty or 0 is refused by the service's validation (service/pipeline/validation.py) before Stage 0, with a 400 and a sentence that says why, under both ways to read the values (median and calibrated) and both modalities. Checked by service tests written first, which fail before the fix
R1_service.before: the scratch probe of 2026-11-10 (a 200-protein, 25-cell table through pipeline.run_projection, protein): every entry empty or NA gave a 200 with every cell left without an answer (observed_genes 0), under both methods; every entry 0 gave a 200 with every cell left without an answer under the calibrated method (verdict unlike_either, read linear, so every 0 missing), and under the median method, the live one, a label for every cell (read log, so every 0 kept as a value)

R1_site.what: the Atlas page's file check (web/js/atlas/file-check.js, checkLimits) turns such a file down before anything is sent, in the same words as the service. The file is not ok, so no question about its values is asked (scale-question.js, asksScale) and Project stays off. Checked by node tests written first, which fail before the fix
R1_site.before: the check passed such a file: its facts line read 'Every value is empty.' (or 100.0% are 0), a protein file was asked raw or log, and the service's 200 followed

R1_walk: valuescale/tests/test_draw.py, written first: a parsed table with no value but 0 or missing is 'empty' after the size checks and before the label; a smaller table keeps its size outcome; a kept linear table whose observed values' 99th percentile is under 64 carries looks_log with its range, and one at or above it carries none; the audit's sample takes every flagged table; a flagged table's packet shows its range, and an unflagged table's packet shows no value
